curated.instructions: omr/instructions/8844-1/ (scans; the helicopter is steps 1-19, pages 4-14; alternate models after, and motorising photos on pages 22-23)

functions.does: The crank low on the left side beside the seats retracts and lowers the landing gear: its 24 tooth gear turns the 8 tooth gear on the end of the front axle, which swings the two front legs fixed on its ends, and a chain from a 16 tooth gear on that axle turns the rear leg's 24 tooth gear, so all three legs swing up or down together.
functions.source: book: steps 1-3 and 5 (front axle, rear leg's gear, chain), steps 6-7 (the crank and its 24 tooth gear), step 19 (the legs and wheels); what it does is inferred from the gears and the chain, as the book draws no arrows

functions.does: The handwheel high on the left side turns the main rotor: a crown gear on its axle drives the 24 tooth gear at the foot of the rotor mast.

The same handwheel turns the tail rotor: a second crown gear on its axle drives an 8 tooth gear on a shaft running back down the tail boom through universal joints to a 16 tooth gear and a crown gear at the tail, whose belt wheel drives the tail rotor's pulley, two round plates, by a rubber band.
functions.source: book: steps 10-12 (the rubber band is in step 11's parts)
functions.note: the rubber band isn't in the model file, so the belt wheel can't drive the tail rotor without it

functions.does: Pushed along, the three wheels roll freely on their axle pins.
The two yellow engines either side of the rotor housing turn freely on their axles.
functions.source: inferred: book step 14 builds them on plain axles through the housing; unsure they are meant to turn

functions.does: The airframe holds its shape: the tail boom and rotor housing, the upright beams behind the seats and the canopy frame of toothed toggle joints all stay fixed to the base whatever is turned.
functions.note: not a control: what every other function needs to hold still

questions.question: Does the crank retract the landing gear? Should the blades be rigid on the hub?
